contributions.statement: When compacting agent history, keep verbatim the spans that likely next steps depend on, plus every failure and state-change span, rather than summarising by recency.
contributions.evidence: Table 1a: AppWorld FOCUS-D 64.9 vs 56.0 no compression (~15 tasks, single seed; rollout ablation swings up to 6pts); OfficeBench +1.1-2.1; non-coding benchmarks, gpt-4.1 only.

contributions.statement: A cheap draft model steering compaction for an expensive main agent can lower total cost.
contributions.evidence: Table 5/12-13: OfficeBench cost -37%; AppWorld advantage smaller; gpt-4.1 draft cost-neutral.

reason: The keep-failure-and-state-spans rule is plausible, but gains are single-seed and comparable to run-to-run swings on non-coding tasks; the cheap-draft-model point is already in the KB.
